source.title: Generation and Analysis of Feature-Dependent Pseudo Noise for Training Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: S. Kamabattula; K. Musini; Babak Namazi; Ganesh Sankaranarayanan; V. Devarajan

record.file_problem: Text appears to contain the full paper; some figures are represented only by captions and descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares learning behavior and test accuracy on randomly relabeled and feature-dependent noisy datasets, using label recall over training as its measure.
record.gate_note: The study tests randomized label noise with specified class-conditional noise distributions at rates 0.2 and 0.5. These are not completely random labelings of the entire training set. Figure-only learning curves are described in the text; rows use the separately reported table values.
record.test_reason: The study measures clean-versus-noisy learning order in new noise settings, directly testing V6. Its randomized-noise experiments also bear on V4: noisy-label recall remains well below one after 200 epochs, establishing incomplete training fit in this setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that Pseudo datasets resemble feature-dependent noise across tested conditions, are easier to fit than matched Randomized datasets, and expose limitations of existing noise-robust training methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ResNet32 with Adam on partially corrupted CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 labels, comparing prescribed class-conditional Randomized noise with feature-dependent Pseudo noise; it does not use completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type (Randomized versus Pseudo), noise rate, dataset, architecture, and learning-rate schedule are varied or discussed as changing learning behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Pseudo-noise checkpoint recalls quantify substantial fitting of feature-dependent incorrect labels, but alone establish neither learning order nor fitting under random corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks substantially fit feature-dependent incorrect labels under standard training.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
record.problems: The reported label-recall table gives only maximum/final test-accuracy checkpoints; learning curves are figure-only. The experiments do not test complete random labeling or zero training error, and the table reports average test accuracy over 3 runs without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table III reports average test-accuracy comparisons for multiple methods. Those results compare methods on noisy-label robustness, rather than directly measuring the versions' named training-fit or learning-order behavior; no separate rows retained.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error on that labeling, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training-time ratios against true-label training and convergence slowdown across increasing random-corruption fractions.
A corruption sweep from zero to complete randomization, steady degradation toward chance over that range, and eventual perfect fit beyond the tested 200-epoch schedule.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Direct identification of shared feature representations or mechanisms underlying the observed learning order.

missing.what: ResNet32 on CIFAR-10 with 0.2 symmetric noise learns clean examples faster initially, then increasingly fits noisy labels while test accuracy declines.
missing.locator: Section I.A, Figure 1; Figure 4 symmetric-noise condition

missing.what: On Red-MiniImageNet at 0.2 noise, clean and noisy learning both begin early, but noisy learning is substantially slower.

The authors report simultaneous early clean/noisy learning for Pseudo noise across CNN9 and ResNet110, constant and alternative decaying learning rates, and a near-symmetric noise distribution at rate 0.18. These conditions extend the scope qualification beyond the retained ResNet32 rows.
A feature-dependent corruption algorithm from prior work is evaluated with ResNet32 on CIFAR-10 at 0.2 noise; noisy-example learning increases later, contrasting with Pseudo noise.

record.verdict_notes: Randomized noise preserves Pseudo noise's class-transition distribution while randomly selecting mislabeled examples; it is not complete independent random labeling. The V4 qualification rests on measured incomplete fit, not on missing measurements. Table III method comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out. Exact learning-curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No result for completely random labeling of the entire training set, zero training error, or unchanged hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training time and convergence slowdown as corrupted-label fraction rises are not reported.
Shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not studied.
Only noise rates 0.2 and 0.5 are compared; no sweep from none to all corruption. The study does not report perfect training-set fit.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not tested as conditions for fitting random labels or generalizing on true labels.
The study compares learning noisy and clean examples over training, but does not test the specific claim that real-label patterns are fit before memorizing random labels in the original settings.

tranche.reason: The matched Randomized-versus-Pseudo comparison explicitly shows conditions requiring V6 to be restated: Pseudo noise is learned alongside clean examples from the beginning. The incomplete Randomized-noise fit also qualifies V4 under the tested schedule.
